newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Moscow to issue Eurobond after March 15.
newsitem.headline: Moscow to issue Eurobond after March 15.

text.p: The City of Moscow will not issue its planned Eurobond until after March 15, the chairman of the city's debt committee said on Monday.
Russian agencies said last week Moscow would issue the bonds by March 15.
But Mstislav Klimovich told Reuters the issue had been delayed because the city was waiting to see government regulations on regional Eurobonds, which are now being drawn up.
"We shall not be able physically to issue the bond by March 15," Klimovich said. "Even if the regulation comes out tomorrow we shall not make it by March 15."
The Russian government is drawing up regulations for regions issuing Eurobond, which among other things will cover taxation of such paper.
Last week the government agreed in principle not to subject regional Eurobonds to a new 15-percent tax on earnings from government securities earnings.
"We are only waiting for an official document," Klimovich said. "That is the only thing which stops us."

On Monday Moody's assigned Moscow a Ba2 credit rating and Standard & Poor's gave it BB minus for the forthcoming bond -- the same as they assigned the Russian Federation for its debut sovereign Eurobond launched last November.
City officials have said Moscow will shortly issue a $400 million Eurobond, which dealers in London say is likely to run for three to five years.
